hunks.baseline: Every now and then, I find myself wondering.
hunks.sol: Every now and then, I found myself wondering.

hunks.baseline: Just how often do I pass out? How many times?
hunks.sol: Just how often did I pass out? How many times had it happened?

hunks.baseline: If the System window summarized my life, how much of it would be time I’d lost while unconscious?
hunks.sol: If the System Window summarized my life, how much of it would I have spent unconscious?

hunks.baseline: Damn it. I have no idea.
hunks.sol: Damn it. I had no idea.

hunks.baseline: The important thing was that I’d just woken up—and found myself face-to-face with some ugly creature that looked like a monster.
hunks.sol: All that mattered right now was that I’d just woken up—and found myself face-to-face with an ugly bastard who looked like a monster.

hunks.baseline: The monster answered in a mumbling voice.
hunks.sol: The monster answered in a mumble.

hunks.baseline: I asked again, baffled.
hunks.sol: Baffled, I asked again.

hunks.baseline: “Is your name Tang Me?”
hunks.sol: “Tang Me?”

hunks.baseline: Captain. The three syllables that came out of the monster’s mouth left me staring with my jaw hanging open.
hunks.sol: *Captain.* The word from the monster’s mouth left my jaw hanging open.

hunks.baseline: When you’re busy with life, it’s easy to forget the little things.
hunks.sol: When you’re busy, it’s easy to forget the little things.

hunks.baseline: Only then did I remember pummeling Hyuk Mujin into the dirt a few days ago. I smiled warmly.
hunks.sol: Only then did I remember beating Hyuk Mujin black and blue a few days ago. I smiled warmly.

hunks.baseline: “Can you see my face right now? That lunatic Taishan hit me before the swelling had even gone down. It got three times worse.”
hunks.sol: “Can you see my face right now? That lunatic Taishan hit me before the swelling had even gone down. It swelled up three times as much.”

hunks.baseline: “Sorry, but I can’t. If I get any closer, I’ll smell your breath. It’s hard enough just standing here as it is.”
hunks.sol: “Sorry, but I can’t. If I get any closer, I’ll smell your breath too. It’s hard enough standing here as it is.”

hunks.baseline: Not until I noticed the terrible stench seeping into my nostrils.
hunks.sol: Then the terrible stench hit my nose.

hunks.baseline: “It really stinks, doesn’t it? Plug your nose with this, like I did, and rinse your mouth out. And try to cover your mouth when you talk, if you can…”
hunks.sol: “It really stinks, doesn’t it? Plug your nose with this, like I did, and rinse your mouth out. And try to cover your mouth when you talk…”

hunks.baseline: Was that idiot Hyuk Mujin actually taking me seriously? Or was he just trying to mess with me even a little?
hunks.sol: Was that idiot Hyuk Mujin actually taking me seriously? Or was he just trying to mess with me?

hunks.baseline: No—if I’m being precise, I’d felt a warmth seep through my body just before I lost consciousness.
hunks.sol: No—to be precise, I’d felt heat seep into my body just before I lost consciousness.

hunks.baseline: A warmth more familiar than anything, as if I’d returned home.
That was why it felt warm rather than hot.
hunks.sol: It had been as familiar as coming home. Warm, rather than hot.

hunks.baseline: Just as not every color in the world is one of the seven colors of the rainbow, energy follows a similar principle.
hunks.sol: Just as the world held more colors than the seven in a rainbow, qi came in more than one kind.

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know how many clans in the world used Scorching Yang Qi, but its roots in the Fire Gate Clan were unmistakable.
hunks.sol: I didn’t know how many sects in the world used Scorching Yang Qi, but the Fire Gate Clan was its root. The qi I’d felt had unquestionably belonged to Jeok Cheongang.

hunks.baseline: The energy I’d felt had unquestionably belonged to Jeok Cheongang.

hunks.baseline: The place was as clean and tidy as when I’d first arrived. But the stench lingering in the air and the dark smudges on the floor were still there.
hunks.sol: The room was as clean and tidy as when I’d first arrived. But the stench lingering in the air and the dark marks on the floor were still there.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin, quick to catch my gaze, complained.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin had caught my gaze and was quick to complain.

hunks.baseline: “According to what the Divine Physician left behind, it was the impurities in your body coming out in a mucus-like form. Um. What exactly did he call it? I knew the word, but it just slipped my mind. Push… push…”
hunks.sol: “The Divine Physician said impurities came out of your body as a kind of mucus. Um, what did he call it? I knew the term, but it’s slipped my mind. Pushing… pushing…”

hunks.baseline: He could only have heard about it. Pushing the meridians and passing through the acupoints required extensive preparation and a willingness to make sacrifices. It wasn’t something people attempted lightly.
hunks.sol: No wonder he’d only heard of it. Pushing the meridians and passing through the acupoints required considerable preparation and sacrifice. It wasn’t something people attempted lightly.

hunks.baseline: But Jeok Cheongang had performed the treatment while I was unconscious, accepting all that risk and the loss of internal energy.
hunks.sol: But Jeok Cheongang had performed the treatment while I was unconscious, accepting the risk and the loss of internal energy.

hunks.baseline: If I’d been hovering between life and death, I might have asked him to. But until now, I’d been getting by just fine.
hunks.sol: If I’d been hovering between life and death, I might have asked him to. But until now, I’d been getting by well enough.

hunks.baseline: I let out a quiet laugh and drew up the Scorching Yang Qi. The increase in my internal energy wasn’t visible, but I could feel it at once.
hunks.sol: I let out a quiet laugh and drew up the Scorching Yang Qi. The increase in my internal energy wasn’t enough to show, but I could feel it at once.

hunks.baseline: Like flowing lava, I spread the Scorching Yang Qi—now a little over three jiazi—through my limbs and every acupoint in my body. At the same time, I quietly surveyed everything deep within me.
hunks.sol: I sent the Scorching Yang Qi—now a little over three jiazi—flowing like lava through every limb and acupoint in my body. At the same time, I quietly examined everything deep within me.

hunks.baseline: My meridians were wider and sturdier. My blood had cleared now that the impurities were gone, and my organs were working normally.
hunks.sol: My acupoints were wider and sturdier. My blood had cleared now that the impurities were gone, and my organs were working normally.

hunks.baseline: The cultivation that had begun as a Small Circulation became a Great Circulation. The fire dragon swept through hundreds of major and minor acupoints, putting my insides in order once more, then finally returned to my lower dantian and coiled up.
hunks.sol: The circulation of qi that had begun as a Small Circulation became a Great Circulation. The fire dragon swept through hundreds of major and minor acupoints, putting my insides in order once more, then finally returned to my lower dantian and coiled up.

hunks.baseline: The effects of that horrible pill the Divine Physician had made and Jeok Cheongang’s treatment must have been the best they could do for me right now.
hunks.sol: That horrible pill the Divine Physician had made and Jeok Cheongang’s treatment must have been the best they could do for me right now.

hunks.baseline: The price for using power my body couldn’t handle was bitter. No matter how much I regretted it, the cold reality wouldn’t change.
hunks.sol: The price of using power my body couldn’t handle was bitter. Wishing otherwise wouldn’t change the reality.

hunks.baseline: A vessel faced with more water than it could hold had only two choices.
hunks.sol: A vessel made to take more water than it could hold had only two possible fates.

hunks.baseline: Hold as much as it could, or break under the weight of the water pouring in.
hunks.sol: It could hold what it was able to—or break under the weight of the water pouring in.

hunks.baseline: I was in the latter situation.
hunks.sol: I was headed for the latter.

hunks.baseline: At my involuntary mutter, Hyuk Mujin, who’d been standing guard, asked,
hunks.sol: At my involuntary mutter, Hyuk Mujin, who’d been standing guard, asked, “Huh? What is?”

hunks.baseline: “Huh? What is?”
I was briefly at a loss for words. Then I shook my head and spoke.
hunks.sol: Briefly at a loss for words, I shook my head.

hunks.baseline: I blinked and asked in a serious voice,
“Are you talking back to me? Is your face itching because you want to be the most handsome man of all time?”
hunks.sol: I blinked and asked in a serious voice, “Are you talking back to me? Is your face itching because you want to be the most handsome man of all time?”

hunks.baseline: “I’m not talking back. I mean it’s going to be difficult time-wise. Everyone’s already prepared and waiting for you to wake up.”
hunks.sol: “I’m not talking back. I mean we don’t have time. Everyone’s ready and waiting for you to wake up.”

hunks.baseline: “…Prepared? Waiting for me to wake up?”
hunks.sol: “…Ready? Waiting for me to wake up?”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. We’ll put up with the smell somehow, so let’s just leave now.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. We’ll put up with the smell somehow, so let’s just leave.”

hunks.baseline: As I stared at him, bewildered, Hyuk Mujin hurriedly rummaged through his robes and pulled out a yellowed sheet of paper.
hunks.sol: As I stared at him, bewildered, Hyuk Mujin hurriedly rummaged through his robes and pulled out a sheet of yellow paper.

hunks.baseline: “It’s a letter Sir Jeok and the Divine Physician left before they departed. They told us to get everything ready and bring you as soon as you woke up, without wasting any time.”
hunks.sol: “It’s a letter Sir Jeok and the Divine Physician left before they departed. They told us to get ready and bring you over as soon as you woke up, without being late.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang and the Divine Physician had left ahead of us. They’d left a letter behind.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang and the Divine Physician had left ahead of us. And they’d left a letter.

hunks.baseline: Trying to make sense of the questions that still wouldn’t go away, I unfolded the rough-textured yellow paper. At that moment, a single line written in a strikingly vigorous hand—presumably the Divine Physician’s—seared itself into my eyes.
hunks.sol: Still full of questions, I unfolded the rough yellow paper. A single line written in a vigorous hand—presumably the Divine Physician’s—seared itself into my eyes.

hunks.baseline: His Master had amassed a fearsome tally of killings—and rescued countless people from the brink of death.
hunks.sol: His Master had taken a fearsome number of lives, yet rescued countless others from the brink of death.

hunks.baseline: *“Tumors too small to see with the naked eye grow deep inside the body. It’s fortunate if you notice the signs early, but unless you can find one of the most renowned physicians, people often die without ever receiving proper treatment.”*
hunks.sol: *“Tumors too small to see with the naked eye grow deep inside the body. You’re fortunate if you notice the signs early, but without a physician of exceptional skill, people often die without ever receiving proper treatment.”*

hunks.baseline: *“You’re not wrong. But if you find a good physician at the right time, it’s an illness you can overcome without needing help from Heaven.”*
hunks.sol: *“You’re not wrong. But if you find the right physician in time, it can be cured without help from Heaven.”*

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: *“Isn’t that because you’re the Divine Physician, and a master of martial arts who’s reached the rank of Grandmaster?”*
hunks.sol: *“Isn’t that because you’re the Divine Physician, and a martial arts master who’s reached the stature of a grandmaster?”*

hunks.baseline: *“Carefully prepare their body for burial, and see them off on their final journey. But whoever the patient may be, always remember one thing.”*
hunks.sol: *“Prepare their body for burial with care, and see them off. But whoever your patient may be, always remember one thing.”*

hunks.baseline: *“There’s no such thing as a death without a cause. Find the cause first.”*
hunks.sol: *“No one dies without a cause. Find the cause first.”*

hunks.baseline: On the broad, lavish bed lay a corpse, sprawled as if in a deep sleep.
hunks.sol: On the broad, lavish bed lay a corpse, as if in a deep sleep.

hunks.baseline: *City Lord of Sichuan Province. What caused your death?*
hunks.sol: *City Lord of Sichuan Province. Why did you die?*

hunks.baseline: Was it the grief of having his beloved concubine taken from him? Or anger at himself for being powerless to stop it?
hunks.sol: Was it grief over having his beloved concubine taken from him? Or anger at himself for being powerless to stop it?

hunks.baseline: The Divine Physician gazed down at the City Lord’s corpse, his eyes calm.
hunks.sol: The Divine Physician gazed calmly down at the City Lord’s corpse.

hunks.baseline: A renowned physician from Sichuan had already concluded that the high-ranking man had died suddenly. But after examining the body for more than three shichen, the Divine Physician disagreed.
hunks.sol: A renowned physician in Sichuan had already decided the high-ranking man’s death had been sudden and natural. But after examining the body for more than three shichen, the Divine Physician disagreed.

hunks.baseline: Along with a question that would never reach the dead man, a long needle was drawn from an acupoint.

hunks.sol: He drew a long needle from an acupoint with a question the dead man would never hear. Then he studied the tiny thing writhing on its sharp tip and murmured,

hunks.sol: “…Gu poison.”
